newsitem.title: USA: New York cheerleader murder accused found dead.
newsitem.headline: New York cheerleader murder accused found dead.

text.p: A New York man who faced the death penalty if found guilty of sexually abusing, killing and spreading the remains of two high school cheerleaders hung himself with a shoe string on Saturday, authorities said.
John Andrews, 31, of Dryden, New York, was found dead in his cell at the Tompkins County Jail at 1:30 a.m. EST (1830 GMT) by a maximum security officer, Sheriff Emery Guest.
Andrews had not been on a "suicide watch" at the prison because a state-required screening concluded that he was not likely to take his own life.
However, several letters were later found in his cell addressed to relatives, indicating he was contemplating suicide, Guest said.
Andrews faced a 26-count indictment that was handed up on Thursday in the deaths of 16-year-old Sarah Hajney and Jennifer Bolduc. He was charged with murder, kidnapping, sexual abuse and burglary.
The teenagers disappeared October 4 from Hajney's home in Dryden where the two girls were house-sitting with a male friend while Sarah's parents were on vacation.

Authorities said Andrews, married with a 6-year-old son, allegedly forced the girls into the family car, killed and dismembered them before scattering body parts over several miles of country roads in Madison and Chenango counties.
Andrews was arrested on Oct. 7 at a Courtland factory where he was a computer lathe operator. He was being held without bail until his scheduled hearing on Wednesday.
